objective: Make the public working-session invitation easier to scan without weakening payment, scope, outcome, continuation, alternate-pathway, privacy, or authority boundaries.

bounded_change.description: Tighten only the proposed public paragraph while retaining the paid 60-minute boundary, problem fit, advance outcome, artifact, stand-alone session, separate continuation decision, and other engagement pathways.

cycle_2.lowest_observed_problem: The proposal described a public/private split but did not make raw source custody a separately testable destination, leaving the private Git sidecar vulnerable to becoming an unrestricted archive.
cycle_2.change: Added an explicit public, private-sidecar, and source-vault placement contract plus adversarial routing tests for identity, quotations, private topology, raw transcripts, and credentials.

cycle_3.lowest_observed_problem: The proposed Contact pathway had no declared editorial owners and no machine-enforced distinction between assignment and acceptance.
cycle_3.change: Assigned Katie Lane, Adrienne R. Fields, and Blair Enns as three fictionalized, public-source-only page-owner lenses with distinct criteria; kept the candidate explicitly unimplemented and unaccepted.

cycle_4.lowest_observed_problem: Adding an unrelated proposed Contact assignment invalidated the Colophon review because its receipt hashed the entire multi-page registry.
cycle_4.change: Bound the existing Colophon receipt to its own assignment plus the shared public-authority boundary, so unrelated page proposals no longer stale it while changes to Colophon still fail closed.

human_gates_remaining: implementation authorization after informed public-repository exposure decision
